hypothesis: H1 for F42: decode right after a long GPU-bank prefill is slower than after a CPU-union prefill of the same prompt because the bank refill looks each routed expert up in the RAM store only once per layer per prompt, so at decode start the 59-slot RAM tier of each layer holds late-first-seen experts with usage 1 and id-ranked pins, while the CPU union re-looks-up every chunk's experts and leaves the prompt tail's experts resident with frequency-ranked pins. Forcing the CPU union with COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH_MIN=100000 (the mirror reserve stays 3100 MiB) should then decode the identical answer faster, through less fetch_wait (fewer RAM misses = O_DIRECT SSD reads) concentrated in the first tokens, with uploads and attach unchanged

notes: Trial vs baseline median: +8.01% (U 2.3030 vs GB 2.1323 tok/s; means 2.2994 vs 2.1197; Welch t = 12.7 on tok/s). Without GB s1 (the first measured sample, serve-unit memory peak 9.7 GiB, an attach outlier) GB is 2.1335 (stdev 0.0027) and U/GB +7.9%.

Decomposition, means over 5+5 samples, GB minus U (decode forwards 1-25 on the server): wall +0.900 s, dec_moe total +0.882 s, fetch_wait +0.826 s, attach +0.060 s (Welch t 0.9: not significant; it comes from GB s1, 3.94 s vs 3.62-3.64 s in the other GB samples and 3.61-3.66 s in U, and is +0.007 s without it), gpu -0.006 s, non-MoE (attention etc.) +0.018 s; uploads -36 (GB 2687, U 2723 in every sample), store misses +608 (GB 1680 vs U 1072, +57%), +7.57 GiB read from SSD. fetch_wait per extra miss: 1.36 ms (one 13.4 MB O_DIRECT read).

Token windows (decode forward j produces content token j+1; means, GB minus U): forwards 1-5: time +347 ms, fetch_wait +315 ms, misses +309, uploads -1, attach +24 ms; 6-10: +242 / +237 / +135 / -8 / -1; 11-24: +297 / +253 / +159 / -18 / +42 (the 11-24 attach is GB s1's; without it -8 ms). Per token: 69, 48 and 21 ms, so front-loaded and decaying but not gone by token 24 (GB still misses 3-18 more experts per forward at forwards 17-25).

RAM tier at decode start (probe v4_dec_res, read under the store mutex): GB holds 59 experts per layer, all with usage 1 (the store saw 103.9 requests per layer: one per routed expert per prompt), 16 pins per layer all with usage 1, ranked by id (exactly the 16 lowest resident ids in 27-29 of 43 layers), 7.9 pins active per layer; U holds 59 per layer with mean usage 7.0 (3.1% at usage <= 1; 1064.9 requests per layer), 16 frequency-ranked pins per layer (median usage 9), all active. Of the experts decode routes in forwards 1-25, 869 of 2192 were resident at decode start in GB vs 1461 of 2207 in U; first forward: 83 of 258 vs 199 of 258. Resident-set overlap GB vs U: Jaccard 0.32.

Routing caveat: although the text is identical, the two prefill paths leave slightly different KV states, so decode routing differs in 430 of 1,075 token-layers (527 of 6,450 expert selections, layers 3-42; deterministic within each arm). This does not drive the gap: swapping routing and RAM sets, GB's routing against U's decode-start RAM finds 1450 experts resident (U's own: 1460) and U's routing against GB's RAM finds 880 (GB's own: 871); on the 645 token-layers with identical routing GB misses 1007 vs U 648.

Strictly one variable: GB and U run the same probe binary with the same server environment except COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH_MIN=100000 in U (sample.txt server_env, engine_environ.txt). Its only read is the bank's per-call gate (hint 1,992 fresh tokens < 100000 -> CPU union); the mirror reserve is sized from COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH and logs 3100 MiB in every sample; GPU0 peaks 21276 vs 21268 MiB.
Probe check: GBn (GB's environment on the unmodified d0e19de2 binary 63a667bac98a..., 3 samples) median 2.1348 tok/s = 1.0012x GB, identical text: the probe changes neither speed nor output.
U's TTFT is 215.2 s vs GB's 82.1 s: the CPU union is the slow prefill PR #1 replaces; this record is about the decode after it, not a recommendation to set COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH_MIN.
